major_concerns: Verifier abstraction mismatch: paper does not yet specify the verifier model, its threat/assumption envelope, or likely false-negative modes.
Calibration generalization risk: calibration tuned on held-out synthetic splits may not generalize to real operator intents.
Simulator fidelity and external validity: simulated ‘apply’ semantics may omit critical runtime state and control-plane interactions.
Human-review workload framing: the <20% threshold is arbitrary and not operationally justified or measured against realistic reviewer capacity.
Insufficient specification of exact public datasets, model identifiers, and prompt templates (hinders reproducibility).
required_design_repairs: Specify exact deterministic verifier implementation (repo/commit), its network model, and known coverage/limitations; include tests showing verifier false-negative/positive rates on representative faults.
Prespecify calibration procedure: exact held-out splits, feature set for confidence, model(s) used, calibration metrics (ECE, ROC), and cross-validation seeds.
Provide concrete public dataset sources and inclusion/exclusion criteria; publish prompt templates and all seeds/prompts/outputs in a reproducible artifact bundle.

Define human-review policy operationally (what constitutes a review request, expected reviewer time per request) and measure reviewer workload impact under realistic assumptions or simulated reviewer models.
Add sensitivity analyses for verifier thresholds, calibration thresholds, and simulator realism; disclose how post-preregistration deviations will be logged.

major_concerns: Risk of iteration oscillation/looping between semantically equivalent failed repairs is not addressed.
Verifier incompleteness: acceptance criteria and verifier false-negative behavior are not quantified and could bias success rates.
Dataset realism: synthetic/crafted repair tasks may not represent production misconfigurations; corpus provenance unclear.
Stopping criterion and retry policy need precise specification to avoid researcher degrees of freedom.
required_design_repairs: Define loop-detection and mitigation (e.g., semantic-diff checks, canonicalization, or provenance-based halting) to prevent oscillation.
Quantify verifier completeness: include oracle-style checks or held-out ‘ground-truth’ repairs to estimate verifier false-negative/positive rates.
Publish exact task-generation procedures or use publicly available benchmark subsets; enumerate fault classes and selection rules.
Prespecify stopping and retry policy (max iterations fixed = 5 stated but include formal justification), seed schedule, temperature, and any prompt-engineering used.
Include per-fault-class power/sample-size justification or acknowledge limits and adopt exact binomial/paired testing corrections for multiple comparisons.

major_concerns: Staged-rollout semantics are underspecified (canary sizing, rollout windows, rollback triggers vary by use case).
Benchmark size (200 tasks) may be too small to support generalizable statistical claims; task selection could bias results.
Simulator fidelity and topology diversity not described; auditability metric is underspecified.
Potential for benchmark to encode specific agent heuristics (overfitting) without cross-validation or external validation.
required_design_repairs: Precisely define staged-rollout primitives (canary percentage, monitoring windows, rollback thresholds) and justify chosen defaults; make them tunable parameters in ablations.
Increase task diversity or provide statistical justification for 200-task corpus; publish task-selection script and seed-controlled splits.
Provide simulator implementation (open-source repo/commit), representative topologies, and validation demonstrating simulator behaviour matches expected control-plane outcomes for canonical cases.
Define auditability metric formally (what constitutes complete provenance) and how it is measured; ensure audit logs are part of the reproducibility artifact.
Include permutation/robustness tests to show benchmark conclusions are not driven by a small subset of tasks; predeclare primary/secondary metrics in preregistration.

major_concerns: Adversarial perturbation realism: threat model and attacker capabilities are not yet specified; perturbations may be unrealistic or trivial.
Ethical and dual-use risk: detailed adversarial prompts could be harmful if published without redaction/safety measures.
Verifier/calibration may generate high false-positive rates under adversarial distributions, harming operational utility—this trade-off is not fully specified.
Reproducibility depends on publishing adversarial generation code but doing so raises safety concerns.
required_design_repairs: Explicitly define attacker threat model (capabilities, knowledge, realistic attack surface) and justify perturbation strategies against that model.
Include an ethical risk mitigation plan: redaction policy for harmful prompts, minimal-disclosure examples, and rationale for public artifact release; consult applicable track/IRB guidance.
Prespecify defender thresholds and study how calibration/verifier thresholds affect false-positive rates in adversarial settings; report ROC/AUC and operationally meaningful operating points.

Release adversarial-generation code with safety filters or provide a vetted, redacted dataset for reproducibility; if full release is unsafe, provide synthetic surrogate generation procedures and seed-controlled configs.
Prespecify logistic-regression model variables, interaction terms, and multiple-comparison corrections in the preregistration.
